results.scientificReason: Urethane formation is a legitimate selected polyaddition example consistent with the neighbouring polyurethane example. The new body requires electron-pair shifts and proton transfer through the linkage, then relates repeated bifunctional reactions to chain formation without eliminating a small molecule. That is a mechanism demand. A product equation, repeat unit or stoichiometric group count alone would not meet it.
results.chemicalBoundary: Alcohol oxygen attacks electrophilic isocyanate carbon; a charge-balanced addition/proton-transfer account yields R–NH–C(=O)–O–Rprime. Catalysts/solvent/transfer partners may change microscopic steps. No universal uncatalysed intramolecular proton jump, radical growth or water elimination is entailed.
